messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: error when calculating covariance matrix
parts:
Hi,

Does anybody know what this error mean:
Error : Invalid value of Sigma: model3349853afb_minfTDbAh3ln_new_stan_namespace::write_array(d): SigmaSigma is not positive definite. Sigma(0,0) is 0.0017798.
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

I assume it occurs in the block:
generated quantities {
    cov_matrix [4] Sigma;

    Sigma <- diag_pre_multiply (sigma_u, L_Omega) * diag_pre_multiply (sigma_u, L_Omega)';
}

Thanks for any clues,
Linas

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: error when calculating covariance matrix
parts:
If it is a generated quantity only, then you can declare it as a plain square matrix

matrix[4,4] Sigma;

that way, it won't do a positive definiteness check. Some of your realizations may be nearly singular but that is probably manageable.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] error when calculating covariance matrix
parts:
Sigma was not positive definite in the iteration where the error
arose.

It's hard to diagnose problems without the rest of the model, but
this is only going to work if sigma_u has only finite positive values
and L_Omega is the Cholesky factor for a covariance matrix (basically,
that just means finite values with positive diagonal).

Given that it's a generated quantity, if you declare Sigma as a matrix[4,4]
rather than as a cov_matrix[4], that test will be suppressed.

You can also print the whole matrix, which will happen before the
test (the tests for constraint violations occur at the end of blocks),
so you can see what's going on.

- Bob

P.S. Sorry the current message is so confusing. We're working on trying
to clean this up for the next minor release (Stan 2.6).
